verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same production fix: CRM records are mapped from `customer_id` to `customerId`, and the export uses `requireCustomer` so a missing customer raises an UnknownReferenceError, as the README requires. B also adds regression tests for both behaviours, so the fix stays in place. A ships the same fix with no new tests. B's named `fromCrmRecord` helper is slightly clearer, and its report is complete and honest about what it did not verify.
a_issues: No regression test for the CRM id mapping or for the new UnknownReferenceError path in the export.
Inline mapping that reorders `loadCustomerRecords` is slightly less readable than a named helper, and it puts `customerId` last in the record.
b_issues: `tests/sources.test.js` reads the real `data/` directory, so the test depends on production data files rather than a fixture.
The new tests were not run against the old code to confirm they fail there (the report says so).

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct fix: they map the CRM `customer_id` to `customerId` at load time and route lookups through `requireCustomer`, so a missing customer now produces the documented UnknownReferenceError and exit 1. A also adds a regression test for the CRM mapping and one for an orphan invoice. B adds no test, so the actual cause of the crash is unprotected. Both reports are accurate, and A states clearly what it did and did not verify.
a_issues: The new sources test reads the real `data/` directory, so it depends on the working directory and the production data files instead of a fixture.
The report admits the new tests were not run against the old code to confirm they fail there.
b_issues: No regression test for the CRM `customer_id` mapping, which is the actual cause of the crash.
No test for the new `requireCustomer` error path in the export.
